Author: Lane #1644 (Codex), 29 October 2026.

These ten lists contain direct mechanism uses selected by resolved Go objects,
method signatures, field stores and actual method sets over workcensus. There
are 421 memberships and 419 distinct canonical sites on the reviewed source.
Transitive callers, unrelated assertions and text hits are discovery context.
Every row records an individual body/consumer decision and pins both the
selected expression and its containing owner. New, removed or changed members
fail TestCapabilityExecutionPopulationCoverage until read and registered.
Discovery never supplies the disposition or reason.

The lists cover configuration handoffs (7), constituent admission (70), direct
capability assertions (68), legacy stored reads (34), exact observed dispatch
(2), Search consumers (39), Engine deletion method sets (16), structural
lookup/unwrap sites (37), read-outcome boundaries (101), and direct stored-fact
owner bodies (47). Engine method-set records include inherited/promoted
methods; declaration-only inspection cannot establish the issued mutation
view. Their contracts record actual compiler method targets and promotion
paths, without inferring behavior from a method's spelling.

The independent structural guard rejects a second wrapper walk even if
registered. Public logical obligations and generated Engine/stored-view
properties provide the behavioral oracles. A test name is only a property
index and cannot approve a disposition. Outside-package controls plant new
renamed/aliased providers and exclude same-named unrelated services.

Separate lists cover 28 typed node-batch bodies in ../foundation-batch-point.tsv,
25 typed entity-ID batch bodies in ../foundation-batch-id-operations.tsv, and
51 errorless data-shaped declarations in ../foundation-legacy-read-apis.json.
Their tests are TestFoundationBatchPointPopulationCoverage,
TestFoundationBatchIDOperationPopulation and TestFoundationLegacyReadPopulation.
The batch-ID list distinguishes read kernels and cancellable sorting from
mutation providers after reading their bodies. The legacy registry distinguishes
42 compatibility declarations from nine poll/copy/control responsibilities.
Public legacy APIs keep their documented omission/zero behavior; the production
compiler/reference gate rejects internal consumers of that compatibility class.

The 16 Engine implementations and 23 stored views retain their separate complete
interface populations, executable factories, logical obligations and independent
public oracles. Readiness additionally requires integrated runtime and source
gates; importing review data alone is not a passing qualification.
